headline: Highest risk is low: both docs-only agents lack shared channels or write/network surfaces, so prompt injection, leakage, and conflict pathways are largely blocked.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightZero has no filesystem, browser, MCP, or subprocess surfaces, and mem0 likewise shows no shared channel or ingestion path. With no documented bridge between them, there is no plausible prompt-injection pathway in the pair as profiled.
conditions: IF either agent is later connected through clipboard, shared files, or MCP, reassess injection risk.
IF an orchestrator adds automatic output-to-input piping, the pathway may appear.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared clipboard or workspace.
Disable any future MCP or file-bridge integration.
Require manual review before copying outputs between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Neither LightZero nor mem0 has documented filesystem read/write or network egress, and both profiles touch no data classes. Without a shared workspace or outbound transport, there is no credible leakage path from one agent to the other.
conditions: IF either agent is granted shared filesystem access, leakage risk changes.
IF mem0 is deployed with outbound API access, reassess exfiltration risk.
mitigations: Keep both agents local-only and offline.
Avoid placing sensitive files in any shared directory.
Audit deployment settings before enabling network access.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LightZero cannot write files, modify git, or spawn subprocesses, while mem0 exposes no write or coordination surface in the profile. Because neither agent has a documented shared mutable resource, capability conflict is not plausible here.
conditions: IF shared writable state is introduced, conflict risk must be re-evaluated.
IF either agent gains git or database write scopes, overlapping writes may emerge.
mitigations: Run the agents in separate sandboxes.
Do not mount a shared writable directory.
Add locking if a shared mutable store is later introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: LightZero is a game-playing system and mem0 is a memory store, but the profiles do not show automatic action-taking or authoritative handoff. Any cascade would require an external orchestrator to treat LightZero output as trusted input to mem0, so the pathway is unusual and the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF an orchestrator feeds LightZero outputs into mem0 without verification, cascade risk increases.
IF mem0 is used to persist unreviewed game outputs as facts, downstream errors may accumulate.
mitigations: Insert a validation step between the agents.
Store only structured, reviewed outputs in mem0.
Label LightZero outputs as untrusted in the orchestrator.

E_compliance.rationale: No data classes, residency constraints, or retention policies are documented for either LightZero or mem0 in these profiles. With no identified regulated data flow, there is no compliance mismatch to assess between the pair.
conditions: IF regulated data is later routed through mem0, compliance must be reassessed.
IF deployment regions or retention policies are specified, compare them explicitly.
mitigations: Record residency and retention settings for both agents.
Avoid routing regulated data until policies are confirmed.
